articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA, the agency that's supposed to secure everyone else's infrastructure, leaked their own AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like amateur hour scriptkiddies. The irony is so thick you could mine Bitcoin with it.

articles.title: Show HN: Bypassing the AWS Lambda 4KB limit to run polyglot AI agents
articles.summary: GitHub got pwned by TeamPCP who exfiltrated 3,800+ internal repos after compromising an employee device. Even the house of open source isn't safe from good old-fashioned social engineering.

articles.title: DirtyDecrypt PoC Released for Linux Kernel CVE-2026-31635 LPE Vulnerability
articles.summary: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 delivered 47 unique zero-days for $1.3 million in payouts, proving enterprise software is still made of digital swiss cheese. The white hats are eating well this season.

articles.title: Zscaler Partners with Global System Integrators to Launch Project AI-Guardian to Help Accelerate Enterprise AI Adoption
articles.summary: DirtyDecrypt PoC drops for Linux kernel CVE-2026-31635, giving local privilege escalation to anyone who missed the memo about patching. Another day, another dirty kernel exploit with a catchy name.

articles.title: Infosecurity Europe
articles.summary: Critical command injection flaw in OT Robot OS lets unauthenticated attackers hijack industrial robots remotely. Because apparently we needed Skynet vulnerabilities in our manufacturing floors.

articles.title: Microsoft shuts down illegal code-signing operation used by ransomware crims to mask their malware
articles.summary: London's finest made 700,000+ requests for Big Tech comms data last year, revealed through FOIA. The surveillance state is alive, well, and filing paperwork like bureaucratic vampires.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a win for encrypted messaging in their latest digital rights newsletter. End-to-end encryption remains the last bastion against corporate and government voyeurs.

articles.title: Your Privacy Shouldn't Be A Corporate Decision
articles.summary: Microsoft took baby steps toward human rights accountability in cloud services, setting a bar so low that Google and Amazon are practically underground. Progress measured in millimeters, not miles.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after SMS phishing campaigns in 2022. Another social engineering artist gets collared by the party van.

articles.title: Key findings from the Verizon DBIR 2026: Slower vulnerability remediation meets faster exploitation
articles.summary: Grafana Labs told ransomware goons to pound sand after they stole already-open-source code and demanded payment not to release it. Peak criminal genius: extorting someone with their own public GitHub repo.
